title: 1 Samuel Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 14.

questions.question: Who accompanied Jonathan when he went to the Philistines' garrison without telling his father?
options: His armourbearer
Saul
Ahiah
Abner
questions.correctAnswer: His armourbearer
questions.explanation: Jonathan said unto the young man that bare his armour to come with him, and he told not his father (1 Samuel 14:1).

questions.question: Where was Saul staying while Jonathan went to the Philistines' garrison?
options: Under a pomegranate tree in Migron
In the city of Gibeah
On Mount Ephraim
At Shiloh
questions.correctAnswer: Under a pomegranate tree in Migron
questions.explanation: Saul tarried in the uttermost part of Gibeah under a pomegranate tree which is in Migron (1 Samuel 14:2).

questions.question: Who was the LORD'S priest in Shiloh wearing an ephod with Saul's army?
options: Ahiah, the son of Ahitub
Ichabod
Phinehas
Eli
questions.correctAnswer: Ahiah, the son of Ahitub
questions.explanation: Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, was the LORD'S priest in Shiloh wearing an ephod (1 Samuel 14:3).

questions.question: What were the names of the two sharp rocks by the passages Jonathan used?
options: Bozez and Seneh
Michmash and Gibeah
Migron and Shiloh
Bethaven and Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: Bozez and Seneh
questions.explanation: There was a sharp rock on one side called Bozez, and the other called Seneh (1 Samuel 14:4).

questions.question: What was the position of the rock named Bozez?
options: Northward over against Michmash
Southward over against Gibeah
Eastward over against Migron
Westward over against Bethaven
questions.correctAnswer: Northward over against Michmash
questions.explanation: The forefront of Bozez was situate northward over against Michmash (1 Samuel 14:5).

questions.question: What reason did Jonathan give to his armourbearer for attacking the Philistines?
options: The LORD can save by many or by few
They wanted to capture the city
They sought revenge for Israel
They were commanded by Saul
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD can save by many or by few
questions.explanation: Jonathan said, 'it may be that the LORD will work for us: for there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few' (1 Samuel 14:6).

questions.question: How did Jonathan's armourbearer respond to his proposal?
options: I am with thee according to thy heart
I will stay behind
I fear the Philistines
We should tell Saul first
questions.correctAnswer: I am with thee according to thy heart
questions.explanation: His armourbearer said, 'Do all that is in thine heart: turn thee; behold, I am with thee according to thy heart' (1 Samuel 14:7).

questions.question: What sign would Jonathan and his armourbearer look for from the Philistines to decide their next move?
options: If the Philistines say 'Come up to us', they would attack
If the Philistines flee, they would retreat
If the Philistines remain silent, they would wait
If the Philistines say 'Tarry until we come to you', they would attack
questions.correctAnswer: If the Philistines say 'Come up to us', they would attack
questions.explanation: Jonathan said if the garrison said 'Come up unto us', then they would go up, for the LORD had delivered them into their hand (1 Samuel 14:10).

questions.question: What did the Philistines say when Jonathan and his armourbearer revealed themselves?
options: Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves
Prepare for battle, the Israelites are here
Retreat quickly to the city
Call your king to aid
questions.correctAnswer: Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves
questions.explanation: The Philistines said, 'Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves' (1 Samuel 14:11).

questions.question: What was the approximate number of men Jonathan and his armourbearer killed in their first attack?
options: About twenty men
About fifty men
About ten men
About one hundred men
questions.correctAnswer: About twenty men
questions.explanation: The first slaughter made by Jonathan and his armourbearer was about twenty men (1 Samuel 14:14).

questions.question: What happened to the Philistine host after Jonathan's attack?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: There was trembling in the host, the earth quaked, and a very great trembling occurred (1 Samuel 14:15).

questions.question: True or False: Saul immediately knew that Jonathan and his armourbearer had left when the people were numbered.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: When they numbered the people, Saul saw that Jonathan and his armourbearer were not there (1 Samuel 14:17).

questions.question: True or False: Ahiah was the captain of Saul's host.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ahiah was the priest, not the captain; Abner was the captain of Saul's host (1 Samuel 14:3, 14:50).

questions.question: True or False: Saul asked Ahiah to bring the ark of God during the battle.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Saul said unto Ahiah, 'Bring hither the ark of God' (1 Samuel 14:18).

questions.question: In the sequence of events in 1 Samuel 14, which happened first?
options: Jonathan and his armourbearer attack the Philistines
Saul commands a food oath on the people
Saul asks Ahiah to bring the ark of God
Jonathan tells his armourbearer to come with him
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan tells his armourbearer to come with him
questions.explanation: Jonathan first asked his armourbearer to go with him to the Philistines' garrison (1 Samuel 14:1), which precedes the other events.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Saul instruct the people to do regarding food until evening, and how did it affect them?
options: He adjured them not to eat any food; the people were distressed and none tasted food.
He commanded them to eat only bread; the people were strengthened for battle.
He told them to drink only water; the people became weak and faint.
He allowed them to eat meat from the spoil; the people were joyful and victorious.
questions.correctAnswer: He adjured them not to eat any food; the people were distressed and none tasted food.
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 14:24, Saul adjured the people not to eat any food until evening so he could be avenged on his enemies, causing distress and fasting among the people. This is further connected to verses 25-26 where the people refrained from eating honey because of the oath.

questions.question: How did Jonathan's actions regarding the honey contrast with Saul's command, and what was the result?
options: Jonathan ate the honey unaware of the oath, and his eyes were enlightened.
Jonathan obeyed the oath and refused to eat the honey, becoming faint.
Jonathan destroyed the honey to prevent others from eating it.
Jonathan warned the people about the oath and they all fasted.
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan ate the honey unaware of the oath, and his eyes were enlightened.
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 14:27 explains that Jonathan did not hear his father's command about the oath, so he ate honey from a honeycomb, which caused his eyes to be enlightened. This contrasts with the other people who refrained from eating because of the oath (verses 24-26).

questions.question: What lesson about leadership and its impact on the people can we learn from Jonathan’s statement in 1 Samuel 14:29?
options: A leader’s decisions deeply affect the well-being and morale of the people.
Leaders should always prioritize military strategy over the people's needs.
Leaders must enforce strict laws without exception to maintain order.
Leaders should separate themselves from the people's struggles.
questions.correctAnswer: A leader’s decisions deeply affect the well-being and morale of the people.
questions.explanation: Jonathan said in verse 29 that his father had troubled the land, showing how Saul's oath negatively affected the people. This teaches that leadership choices profoundly influence the people's condition and morale (verses 24, 29).

questions.question: What did Saul command after learning that the people had eaten meat with the blood, and why?
options: He commanded them to kill their animals properly and not eat blood, as they had sinned against the LORD.
He allowed them to continue eating the meat as long as they repented afterward.
He ignored the sin and focused on pursuing the Philistines.
He ordered a fast to atone for the sin of eating with the blood.
questions.correctAnswer: He commanded them to kill their animals properly and not eat blood, as they had sinned against the LORD.
questions.explanation: In verses 33-34, Saul responded to the sin of eating meat with blood by instructing the people to bring their animals and kill them properly to avoid sinning against the LORD, showing concern for obedience and holiness.

questions.question: What significant religious act did Saul perform after the battle, and what was its importance?
options: He built an altar to the LORD; it was the first altar he built.
He destroyed the altar of the Philistines to show victory.
He offered a burnt sacrifice on the battlefield before the fight.
He built a temple in Gibeah to honor God.
questions.correctAnswer: He built an altar to the LORD; it was the first altar he built.
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 14:35 states that Saul built an altar to the LORD, marking the first altar he built, signifying a formal act of worship and thanksgiving after the battle.

questions.question: How did Saul seek God's guidance before pursuing the Philistines by night, and what was the outcome?
options: He asked God if he should pursue, but God did not answer that day.
He prayed and received a clear sign to attack immediately.
He consulted the people instead of God and decided to pursue.
He ignored seeking God's counsel and went ahead with the attack.
questions.correctAnswer: He asked God if he should pursue, but God did not answer that day.
questions.explanation: In verses 36-37, Saul proposed to pursue the Philistines by night and asked God for guidance through the priest, but God did not answer him that day, indicating a lack of divine confirmation.

questions.question: What was the purpose of Saul drawing near the people to identify the sin that caused God's silence, according to 1 Samuel 14:38-39?
options: To find out who had broken the oath about eating food and bring judgment.
To find a traitor among the people allied with the Philistines.
To select a leader to replace his son Jonathan.
To decide which soldiers should be sent to the front lines.
questions.correctAnswer: To find out who had broken the oath about eating food and bring judgment.
questions.explanation: Verses 38-39 describe Saul gathering the chiefs to discover the sin responsible for God's silence. He declared that the offender, even if it was Jonathan, must die, showing the seriousness of obedience.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 14:40-41, how was the guilty party identified?
options: By casting lots between Saul and Jonathan, and Jonathan was taken.
By confession of the people, and Jonathan admitted his fault.
By the priest's prophecy, revealing Jonathan's guilt.
By Saul's personal investigation and witness testimony.
questions.correctAnswer: By casting lots between Saul and Jonathan, and Jonathan was taken.
questions.explanation: Verses 40-42 explain that Saul separated himself and Jonathan from the people and cast lots to determine who was guilty. The lot fell on Jonathan, identifying him as the offender.

questions.question: What was Saul's initial reaction to Jonathan's confession about eating honey, and what was the people's response?
options: Saul insisted Jonathan must die, but the people opposed and saved him.
Saul forgave Jonathan immediately, and the people rejoiced.
Saul ignored the confession, and the people demanded punishment.
Saul punished Jonathan publicly, and the people agreed.
questions.correctAnswer: Saul insisted Jonathan must die, but the people opposed and saved him.
questions.explanation: In verses 43-45, Jonathan admitted eating honey, and Saul declared he must die. However, the people defended Jonathan, saying he had wrought great salvation, preventing his death.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 14:46 describe the conclusion of the battle and its immediate aftermath?
options: Saul ceased pursuing the Philistines, who returned to their own land.
Saul chased the Philistines until they were completely destroyed.
The Philistines captured Saul and his army.
Saul's army retreated, and the Philistines advanced.
questions.correctAnswer: Saul ceased pursuing the Philistines, who returned to their own land.
questions.explanation: Verse 46 states that Saul stopped following the Philistines, who then went back to their own place, marking the end of that particular confrontation.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 14:47 teach about Saul’s reign in terms of his military campaigns?
options: Saul fought against all his enemies on every side and vexed them wherever he turned.
Saul avoided battles and sought peace with neighboring nations.
Saul only fought the Philistines and ignored other enemies.
Saul lost many battles and was often defeated.
questions.correctAnswer: Saul fought against all his enemies on every side and vexed them wherever he turned.
questions.explanation: Verse 47 summarizes Saul’s reign as marked by constant warfare against various enemies, including Moab, Ammon, Edom, Zobah, and the Philistines, showing his active defense of Israel.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Samuel 14:19, Saul told the priest to withdraw his hand because the noise from the Philistines was increasing.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 19 states that while Saul was talking to the priest, the noise in the Philistine camp increased, prompting Saul to tell the priest to withdraw his hand.

questions.question: True or False: The people refused to participate in the casting of lots to find the sinner who broke the oath in 1 Samuel 14:39.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 39 records that no one among the people answered Saul regarding the sin, indicating silence, but they did not refuse participation in the casting of lots described in verses 40-42.

questions.question: True or False: The priest encouraged Saul and the people to draw near to God before pursuing the Philistines by night, as recorded in 1 Samuel 14:36.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In verse 36, after Saul proposed the night attack, the priest said, 'Let us draw near hither unto God,' encouraging seeking God's presence before battle.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 14:30 suggest about the impact if the people had eaten food earlier during the battle?
options: There would have been a much greater slaughter of the Philistines.
The people would have been weaker and defeated.
The battle would have ended in a stalemate.
The Philistines would have captured the Israelites.
questions.correctAnswer: There would have been a much greater slaughter of the Philistines.
questions.explanation: Jonathan speculated in verse 30 that if the people had eaten earlier, there would have been a greater slaughter of the Philistines, indicating the importance of physical strength and provision in battle.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 14.

questions.question: What was Saul's response when asked if Jonathan should die for breaking the oath about eating food?
options: He spared Jonathan immediately
He insisted Jonathan must die
He ignored the question
He asked the people what to do
questions.correctAnswer: He insisted Jonathan must die
questions.explanation: Saul declared that Jonathan shall surely die for breaking the oath, as stated in 1 Samuel 14:44.

questions.question: How did the people react to Saul's decision to punish Jonathan for eating honey?
options: They agreed Jonathan should die
They rescued Jonathan and prevented his death
They remained silent
They rebelled against Saul
questions.correctAnswer: They rescued Jonathan and prevented his death
questions.explanation: The people said Jonathan should not die because he had wrought great salvation that day, and they rescued him so he did not die (1 Samuel 14:45).

questions.question: What was the result of Saul casting lots between himself and Jonathan?
options: Saul was taken
Jonathan was taken
Both were taken
Neither was taken
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan was taken
questions.explanation: Saul cast lots between himself and Jonathan, and Jonathan was taken (1 Samuel 14:42).

questions.question: What did Saul do after the battle and after the people sinned by eating meat with blood?
options: He ignored the sin
He built an altar to the LORD
He punished the people severely
He fled from the battle
questions.correctAnswer: He built an altar to the LORD
questions.explanation: After the people sinned by eating meat with blood, Saul built the first altar to the LORD as recorded in 1 Samuel 14:35.

questions.question: What was the oath Saul made to his people before the battle?
options: Not to drink water until evening
Not to eat any food until evening
Not to fight until morning
Not to retreat under any circumstance
questions.correctAnswer: Not to eat any food until evening
questions.explanation: Saul adjured the people, saying cursed be the man that eateth any food until evening (1 Samuel 14:24).

questions.question: What was Jonathan's reasoning when he tasted the honey despite his father's oath?
options: He did not hear the oath
He wanted to rebel
He was hungry
He forgot about the oath
questions.correctAnswer: He did not hear the oath
questions.explanation: Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath, so he tasted the honey (1 Samuel 14:27).

questions.question: What was the sign Jonathan and his armourbearer used to decide whether to attack the Philistine garrison?
options: If Philistines shouted 'Come up to us', they would attack
If Philistines fled, they would attack
If the sun was high, they would attack
If the priest gave a sign, they would attack
questions.correctAnswer: If Philistines shouted 'Come up to us', they would attack
questions.explanation: Jonathan said if the Philistines say 'Come up to us', then they would go up because the LORD hath delivered them (1 Samuel 14:10).

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word 'ephod' mentioned in the chapter in relation to Ahiah?
options: A priestly garment used for seeking God's counsel
A weapon used in battle
A musical instrument
A type of armor
questions.correctAnswer: A priestly garment used for seeking God's counsel
questions.explanation: Ahiah, the priest, wore an ephod, which in Hebrew tradition is a priestly garment used often when seeking God's counsel (1 Samuel 14:3).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage similarly involves casting lots to determine God's will, connecting to the casting of lots in 1 Samuel 14:41-42?
options: Leviticus 16:8
Joshua 7:14
Exodus 12:5
Numbers 22:8
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua 7:14
questions.explanation: Joshua 7:14 describes casting lots to find the sinner among Israel, a method of discerning God's will like in 1 Samuel 14:41-42.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in the parallel division of the people into two sides: Saul and Jonathan on one, and all Israel on the other, as in 1 Samuel 14:40?
options: Chiasm
Parallelism
Inclusio
Foreshadowing
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: The division into two opposing sides reflects parallelism, a common Hebrew literary device emphasizing contrast (1 Samuel 14:40).

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 14:37, what was God's response when Saul asked if he should pursue the Philistines that day?
options: God said yes
God said no
God did not answer
God sent a prophet
questions.correctAnswer: God did not answer
questions.explanation: Saul asked counsel of God, but God answered him not that day (1 Samuel 14:37).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's deliverance by few, as Jonathan expressed in 1 Samuel 14:6?
options: 1 Corinthians 1:27
Romans 8:28
Hebrews 11:34
Acts 2:17
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Corinthians 1:27
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:27 talks about God choosing the weak and foolish to shame the strong, echoing Jonathan's faith that the LORD can save by many or few (1 Samuel 14:6).

questions.question: What was the reason Saul gave for building the altar to the LORD after the battle (1 Samuel 14:35)?
options: To commemorate the victory over the Amalekites
It was the first altar he built to the LORD
To seek forgiveness for the oath violation
To dedicate his kingdom to God
questions.correctAnswer: It was the first altar he built to the LORD
questions.explanation: The text states that the altar Saul built was the first altar he built unto the LORD (1 Samuel 14:35).

questions.question: True or False: The people of Israel agreed with Saul that Jonathan must die for eating honey.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The people rescued Jonathan and said he should not die because he had wrought great salvation (1 Samuel 14:45).

questions.question: True or False: The chapter shows that Saul's failure to hear from God led to a legalistic approach to sin rather than mercy.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: God did not answer Saul (1 Samuel 14:37), and Saul insisted Jonathan must die for the oath violation, showing a strict, legalistic approach (1 Samuel 14:39-44).

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by Jonathan's confidence that the LORD can save "by many or by few" in attacking the Philistine garrison?
options: God’s omnipotence
God’s omnipresence
God’s immutability
God’s jealousy
questions.correctAnswer: God’s omnipotence
questions.explanation: Jonathan states there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few, showing God's unlimited power (1 Samuel 14:6). This reveals the attribute of God's omnipotence.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is highlighted by Saul’s imposition of a curse forbidding his army to eat until evening during battle?
options: Doctrine of sanctification through obedience
Doctrine of divine wrath
Doctrine of covenant faithfulness
Doctrine of human free will
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of sanctification through obedience
questions.explanation: Saul’s oath to avoid food until victory reflects a call to holiness and obedience, illustrating sanctification as separation unto God’s purpose (1 Samuel 14:24).

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 14:18-19, Saul asks Ahiah to bring the ark of God. What does this action reveal about Saul’s understanding of God’s presence and guidance in battle?
options: Saul believes the physical presence of the ark ensures victory
Saul is seeking God’s direct guidance and favor in uncertain circumstances
Saul wants to intimidate the Philistines with the ark
Saul uses the ark as a talisman for good luck
questions.correctAnswer: Saul is seeking God’s direct guidance and favor in uncertain circumstances
questions.explanation: By requesting the ark, Saul seeks divine guidance and intervention, acknowledging God’s presence as essential for victory (1 Samuel 14:18-19).

questions.question: How does Jonathan’s action of tasting honey despite Saul’s oath (1 Samuel 14:27-29) theologically illustrate the tension between human oath and divine provision?
options: It shows human oaths are always above God’s provision
It demonstrates that God’s provision sustains life and can override human restrictions
It proves that Jonathan was disobedient without consequence
It indicates that Saul’s leadership was divinely approved
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates that God’s provision sustains life and can override human restrictions
questions.explanation: Jonathan’s eyes were enlightened after tasting honey, showing that God’s provision is necessary for strength and can supersede human vows (1 Samuel 14:27-29).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do 1 Samuel 14:13-14 and 1 Samuel 14:23 convey about God’s salvation in battle?
options: Salvation depends on human strength and numbers
God’s salvation is sovereign and can work through few to defeat many
Victory in battle is guaranteed by military strategy alone
God’s salvation is only for Israel’s political expansion
questions.correctAnswer: God’s salvation is sovereign and can work through few to defeat many
questions.explanation: Jonathan and his armourbearer slew about twenty men, and the LORD saved Israel that day, showing salvation is by God’s sovereign power, not human might (1 Samuel 14:13-14, 23).

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 14:39-42 illustrate the theological principle of corporate responsibility and individual accountability within Israel’s community?
options: Only leaders are held accountable for sin
Community bears responsibility but individuals must answer for personal actions
Individual actions have no impact on the community
Collective guilt is ignored in favor of personal guilt
questions.correctAnswer: Community bears responsibility but individuals must answer for personal actions
questions.explanation: Saul declares Jonathan must die for breaking the oath, yet the people intervene to save him, demonstrating both corporate and individual accountability (1 Samuel 14:39-42).

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed by His silence to Saul’s inquiry about pursuing the Philistines at night (1 Samuel 14:37)?
options: God’s faithfulness
God’s inscrutability
God’s mercy
God’s omniscience
questions.correctAnswer: God’s inscrutability
questions.explanation: God’s lack of response to Saul’s question highlights divine mystery and inscrutability in His timing and purposes (1 Samuel 14:37).

questions.question: What narrative arc does 1 Samuel 14:47-48 contribute to the broader biblical story of Israel’s monarchy and God’s covenantal faithfulness?
options: Saul’s failures lead to the end of Israel’s monarchy
Saul’s military successes demonstrate God’s ongoing covenantal protection
Israel’s monarchy is established by human conquest alone
God abandons Israel due to Saul’s sin
questions.correctAnswer: Saul’s military successes demonstrate God’s ongoing covenantal protection
questions.explanation: Saul’s victories against enemies show God’s covenantal faithfulness to protect Israel through the monarchy (1 Samuel 14:47-48).

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about sin and atonement is taught by Saul’s command to slaughter animals and eat them without blood in 1 Samuel 14:33-34?
options: Blood is irrelevant in sin and atonement
Eating blood is a sin against the LORD and must be avoided
Slaughtering animals is unnecessary for atonement
Sin is only external and not related to dietary laws
questions.correctAnswer: Eating blood is a sin against the LORD and must be avoided
questions.explanation: Saul identifies eating with blood as sin and commands proper slaughtering to avoid defiling the people, affirming blood’s sacred role in atonement (1 Samuel 14:33-34).

questions.question: How do 1 Samuel 14:20-22 demonstrate God’s providential control even over human confusion and enemy defeat?
options: God causes intentional confusion among His people
God works providentially as enemies turn on one another and Israel pursues them
Human skill alone brings victory
The battle results from chance and chaos without divine involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God works providentially as enemies turn on one another and Israel pursues them
questions.explanation: The text describes men’s swords against each other and Israel pursuing the fleeing Philistines, showing God’s providential hand in confusing enemies (1 Samuel 14:20-22).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the events in 1 Samuel 14 show human military prowess rather than divine intervention. What does 1 Samuel 14:11-15 actually teach about God’s role in Israel’s victory?
options: Victory was due to Jonathan’s strategic skill alone
God caused trembling and confusion among the enemy, enabling victory
The battle was won by sheer numbers and weapons
The Philistines surrendered voluntarily without divine influence
questions.correctAnswer: God caused trembling and confusion among the enemy, enabling victory
questions.explanation: Verses 14-15 describe a great trembling and the earth quaking, indicating God’s supernatural intervention in Israel’s victory (1 Samuel 14:11-15).

questions.question: What theological synthesis emerges when combining 1 Samuel 14:1-3 and 1 Samuel 14:46 regarding God’s providence and human initiative in salvation history?
options: God works without any human participation
Human initiative is primary and God’s providence is secondary
God’s providence works through human initiative for salvation
Human actions can override God’s plan
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence works through human initiative for salvation
questions.explanation: Jonathan’s secret initiative and the subsequent victory show that God’s providence often operates through human actions in salvation history (1 Samuel 14:1-3, 46).

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 14:35 reveal about Saul’s relationship with God through the act of building an altar?
options: It marks Saul’s formal dedication and worship of God
It shows Saul’s rejection of God
It is a pagan ritual adopted by Saul
It indicates Saul’s reliance on military power only
questions.correctAnswer: It marks Saul’s formal dedication and worship of God
questions.explanation: Saul building an altar to the LORD is his first altar, signifying his intention to honor and worship God formally (1 Samuel 14:35).

questions.question: Which of the following best expresses the doctrinal significance of 1 Samuel 14:49-50 regarding the roles within Israel’s leadership and family structure?
options: Leadership is unrelated to family lineage
Leadership and family roles are intertwined, with military and royal responsibilities
Only priests have leadership roles in Israel
Women held primary military command
questions.correctAnswer: Leadership and family roles are intertwined, with military and royal responsibilities
questions.explanation: The passage lists Saul’s sons, daughters, wife, and the captain of his host, showing leadership roles connected with family and military (1 Samuel 14:49-50).

questions.question: What synthesis about divine judgment and mercy can be drawn from 1 Samuel 14:39 and 1 Samuel 14:45 concerning Jonathan’s near execution?
options: God’s judgment is final without mercy
God’s judgment may come through human leaders but mercy can be exercised by the community
God’s mercy overrides all judgment
Jonathan’s actions were without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment may come through human leaders but mercy can be exercised by the community
questions.explanation: Saul pronounces death on Jonathan (judgment), but the people rescue him (mercy), illustrating tension between divine judgment and communal mercy (1 Samuel 14:39, 45).
